APCTT-C01.quote: For each shoreline position, the total uncertainty is found as the square root of the sum of squares (Taylor, 1997) of the relevant uncertainty terms, based on an assumption that each term is random and independent of the others.
APCTT-C01.note: Statistical basis of the rates and uncertainty terms, with cited methods (Crowell and others, 1993; Hapke and others).

APCTT-C02.quote: One purpose of this work is to develop standard, repeatable methods for mapping and analyzing shoreline change so that periodic, systematic, and internally consistent updates regarding coastal erosion and land loss can be made nationally.

APCTT-C03.quote: Shoreline change rates were derived from 26,567 individual transects, of which 84 percent were erosional.

APCTT-C05.quote: To verify T-sheets and datum transformations, a comparison was made between the georeferenced T-sheets, georeferenced 2000s era imagery, and published locations of the NGS benchmark locations, which were mapped on and used as survey control for the T-sheets.
APCTT-C05.note: Borderline: verification of inputs against benchmarks and stable features in the study area; uncertainty quantified (p26).

APCTT-C06.quote: Shoreline change was evaluated by comparing historical shorelines derived from circa-1940s (1947 and 1949) topographic surveys and circa-2000s (1997–2012) vertical aerial photography, satellite imagery, and digital elevation models derived from lidar (light detection and ranging) surveys
APCTT-C06.note: Workflow applied to the Alaska north coast.

APCTT-C07.quote: This report on shoreline change along the north coast of Alaska, between the U.S.-Canadian border and Icy Cape, is one in a series of regionally focused reports on historical shoreline change.
APCTT-C07.note: Used within the operational National Assessment of Shoreline Change programme, with previous regional reports for other U.S. coasts.

APCTT-C09.note: Borderline: part of a long-running national series, but no stated period of operation of this workflow.

APCTT-C10.note: Accuracy standards are cited for input data, but measured performance is not compared with stated requirements.

APCTT-C11.quote: No distinction was made between sand or gravel beaches, and the base of the unconsolidated coastal bluff was considered the shoreline where no fronting beach existed.
APCTT-C11.note: Shoreline proxy, periods, data sources and their accuracies defined.

APCTT-C12.quote: Shoreline change rates were derived from 26,567 individual transects, of which 84 percent were erosional.
APCTT-C12.note: Evidence concerns the Alaska shoreline-change workflow.
